questions.q: Who does Isaiah say will experience trouble because of their unjust laws and decrees?
questions.a: Judges and rulers who make unjust laws and decrees that cause people to suffer will experience trouble.

questions.q: What do these unjust rulers do to widows and orphans?
questions.a: They deny justice to poor and needy people, seize what belongs to widows, and rob orphans of their possessions.

questions.q: What will the unjust rulers be unable to do when Yahweh sends an army from far away to punish them?
questions.a: They will be unable to save themselves, unable to run to anyone for help, and will have nowhere to keep their valuable possessions safe.

questions.q: Even though Yahweh is still angry, what will happen to the people?
questions.a: The people will stumble along as prisoners, or their dead bodies will fall among those whom others have killed.

questions.q: Who does Yahweh use like a rod and a club to punish the nations he is angry with?
questions.a: Yahweh uses Assyria like a rod and a club to punish the nations with which he is angry.

questions.q: What did Yahweh command the Assyrian to do to the nation with which he was angry?
questions.a: Yahweh commanded the Assyrian to take away their valuable possessions and to trample them like mud in the streets.

questions.q: What did the Assyrian intend?
questions.a: It was in the Assyrian’s heart to destroy and eliminate many nations.

questions.q: What does the king of Assyria boast about his commanders?
questions.a: He boasts that all his commanders are kings he has conquered.

questions.q: What cities does the king of Assyria boast that he has conquered?
questions.a: He boasts that he has conquered Calno, Carchemish, Hamath, Arpad, Samaria, and Damascus.

questions.q: What does the king of Assyria say about the idols of the kingdoms he conquered?
questions.a: He says their idols were more impressive than the idols in Jerusalem and Samaria.

questions.q: What does the king of Assyria threaten to do to Jerusalem?
questions.a: He threatens to do to Jerusalem and its gods what he did to Samaria and its gods.

questions.q: What did the Lord say he would do when he finished his work on Mt. Zion and in Jerusalem?
questions.a: The Lord said he would punish the king of Assyria, because the king was very proud and looked at everyone with arrogant contempt.

questions.q: Why did the king of Assyria think he was successful?
questions.a: The king of Assyria thought he was successful because of his own strength, wisdom, and understanding.

questions.q: To what does the king of Assyria compare taking the wealth of other kingdoms?
questions.a: He compares it to someone easily reaching into a bird’s nest and gathering abandoned eggs, with no bird flapping its wings or chirping to stop him.

questions.q: What does Yahweh say an axe or a saw cannot do?
questions.a: Yahweh says an axe cannot boast that it is stronger than the person who chops with it, and a saw cannot claim to be greater than the person who moves it.

questions.q: What was the Lord God going to do among Assyria’s elite warriors?
questions.a: The Lord God was going to cause Assyria’s strong warriors to become very thin from disease.

questions.q: How quickly will Yahweh destroy the Assyrians, according to this verse?
questions.a: Yahweh will destroy the Assyrians in a single day, as if burning up thorns and briars with fire.

questions.q: What did Yahweh say he would consume in Assyria?
questions.a: Yahweh said he would completely destroy the splendid forests and fertile farmlands of Assyria.

questions.q: How many trees will remain in the forests of Assyria?
questions.a: So few trees will remain that even a child could count them.

questions.q: What would the remnant of Israel rely upon after they escape?
questions.a: The remnant that survived would no longer rely on the Assyrians who attacked them, but would genuinely trust in Yahweh.

questions.q: What will the remnant of Jacob do?
questions.a: The remnant of Jacob will return to worship the Mighty God.

questions.q: How many of the people of Israel will return, even though they are as numerous as the sand of the sea?
questions.a: Only a small remnant of them will return; Yahweh has determined to destroy most of them because of their sins.

questions.q: What has Yahweh determined to do throughout the world?
questions.a: Yahweh has determined to bring an end and to destroy people throughout the world.

questions.q: Why did the Lord God tell the people who lived in Zion not to fear the Assyrian?
questions.a: He told them not to fear the Assyrian because in a very short time the Lord’s anger against those in Zion would end and the Lord’s anger would be toward Assyria’s destruction.

questions.q: To what past events does Yahweh compare his defeat of Assyria?
questions.a: Yahweh compares it to his defeat of the Midianites at the rock of Oreb and his destruction of the Egyptian army at the sea.

questions.q: What would happen to the people’s burden and yoke on the day Yahweh defeated Assyria?
questions.a: On that day their burden would be lifted from their shoulders and their yoke removed from their necks; they would no longer be slaves to the Assyrians.

questions.q: Where does the Assyrian army store its equipment?
questions.a: The Assyrian army stores its equipment at Michmash.

questions.q: How do the people of Ramah and Gibeah respond to the approaching Assyrian army?
questions.a: The people of Ramah tremble with fear, and the people of Gibeah, King Saul’s hometown, run away.

questions.q: What should the people of Gallim and Laishah do as the Assyrian army approaches?
questions.a: The people of Gallim should cry out for help, and the people of Laishah should listen to them.

questions.q: What do the people of Madmenah and Gebim do as the Assyrian army approaches?
questions.a: The people of Madmenah run away, and the people of Gebim try to hide.

questions.q: Where will the Assyrian army halt on that day?
questions.a: The Assyrian army will halt at Nob and shake its fist to threaten the people of Jerusalem on Mount Zion.

questions.q: What does Yahweh compare his defeat of the proud Assyrian soldiers to?
questions.a: Yahweh compares it to cutting down tall, proud trees with terrifying power.

questions.q: What does Yahweh use to cut down the forest and Lebanon?
questions.a: Yahweh uses his great power, as if it were an iron axe, to cut down the forest and the great trees of Lebanon.

commentary.text: Woes against proud oppressors. (Is. 10:1-4) The Assyrian but an instrument in the hand of God for the punishment of his people. (Is. 10:5-19) The deliverance from him. (Is. 10:20-34)

Is. 10:1-4 These verses are to be joined with the foregoing chapter. Woe to the superior powers that devise and decree unrighteous decrees! And woe to the inferior officers that draw them up, and enter them on record! But what will sinners do? Whither will they flee?

Is. 10:5-19 See what a change sin made. The king of Assyria, in his pride, thought to act by his own will. The tyrants of the world are tools of Providence. God designs to correct his people for their hypocrisy, and bring them nearer to him; but is that Sennacherib's design? No; he designs to gratify his own covetousness and ambition. The Assyrian boasts what great things he has done to other nations, by his own policy and power. He knows not that it is God who makes him what he is, and puts the staff into his hand. He had done all this with ease; none moved the wing, or cried as birds do when their nests are rifled. Because he conquered Samaria, he thinks Jerusalem would fall of course. It was lamentable that Jerusalem should have set up graven images, and we cannot wonder that she was excelled in them by the heathen. But is it not equally foolish for Christians to emulate the people of the world in vanities, instead of keeping to things which are their special honour? For a tool to boast, or to strive against him that formed it, would not be more out of the way, than for Sennacherib to vaunt himself against Jehovah. When God brings his people into trouble, it is to bring sin to their remembrance, and humble them, and to awaken them to a sense of their duty; this must be the fruit, even the taking away of sin. When these points are gained by the affliction, it shall be removed in mercy. This attempt upon Zion and Jerusalem should come to nothing. God will be as a fire to consume the workers of iniquity, both soul and body. The desolation should be as when a standard-bearer fainteth, and those who follow are put to confusion. Who is able to stand before this great and holy Lord God?

Is. 10:20-34 By our afflictions we may learn not to make creatures our confidence. Those only can with comfort stay upon God, who return to him in truth, not in pretence and profession only. God will justly bring this wasting away on a provoking people, but will graciously set bounds to it. It is against the mind and will of God, that his people, whatever happens, should give way to fear. God's anger against his people is but for a moment; and when that is turned from us, we need not fear the fury of man. The rod with which he corrected his people, shall not only be laid aside, but thrown into the fire. To encourage God's people, the prophet puts them in mind of what God had formerly done against the enemies of his church. God's people shall be delivered from the Assyrians. Some think it looks to the deliverance of the Jews out of their captivity; and further yet, to the redemption of believers from the tyranny of sin and Satan. And this, "because of the anointing;" for his people Israel's sake, the believers among them that had received the unction of Divine grace. And for the sake of the Messiah, the Anointed of God. Here is, Is. 10:28-34, a prophetical description of Sennacherib's march towards Jerusalem, when he threatened to destroy that city. Then the Lord, in whom Hezekiah trusted, cut down his army like the hewing of a forest. Let us apply what is here written, to like matters in other ages of the church of Christ. Because of the anointing of our great Redeemer, the yoke of every antichrist must be broken from off his church: and if our souls partake of the unction of the Holy Spirit, complete and eternal deliverances will be secured to us.
